snapshot.title: New global AI computing capacity is doubling every 9 months
paragraphs: Each quarter adds more computing capacity than the last, at a pace of roughly 2.5× a year since 2024. That is slower than 2023, when capacity additions jumped about sixfold after ChatGPT and GPT-4 launched and Nvidia’s H100 arrived.
There are hints of a further slowdown, though the signal is not statistically significant and could simply be a pause between chip generations.

steps.title: A sixfold surge
steps.text: After ChatGPT and GPT-4 launched and Nvidia’s H100 arrived, quarterly additions of AI computing capacity grew roughly 6× in a single year.

steps.title: Steady growth of 2.5× a year
steps.text: Growth has settled to about 2.5× per year, with a 90% confidence interval of 2.3× to 2.7×.

steps.title: Doubling every 9 months
steps.text: At 2.5× a year, the amount of new computing capacity added each quarter doubles roughly every nine months.

steps.title: A slowdown? Not yet clear
steps.text: Some evidence points to further deceleration, but it is not statistically significant and may reflect a lull between chip generations, such as the wait for Nvidia’s Rubin.
